universal-anime-system.summary: UAS is a sandbox tabletop system designed for modular adaptation across anime, fantasy and other settings. First-edition materials center backstory-driven character creation, stackable backgrounds/proficiencies, custom powers/spells, a rank-scaled difficulty model, Action Point combat, equipment proficiency and highly modular combat classes/subclasses.
systems: Action Point economy with Dexterity scaling
Combat roles including Guardian, Artillery, Tactician, Operative, Bruiser, Aid and Diplomat with subclasses
unresolved_questions: How much of first-edition prose/mechanics survived into UAS SYSTEM 2nd Edition?
Retry inaccessible UAS - Origins sheet and reconcile against earlier UAS Origin System.

second_edition.summary: Second Edition moved UAS from prose-heavy first-edition rules into a spreadsheet-driven rules engine and reusable data model. Core tabs cover rank/modifier math, item/damage classes, skills/proficiencies, level progression, player classes/subclasses, status effects, encounter scaling, exports and a system wiki.
mechanics: D-to-EX master rank table drives DCs, MP, spell-point cost, dice, armor, loot value and encounter difficulty points.
Actions are decomposed by action economy, target shape, action type, mastery and defensive modifiers.
Level progression through 20 raises rank, stat budget/caps, proficiency, feats, skill proficiencies, spell-point limits, spell ranks, ultimates and class/subclass feats.
Seven combat roles remain Guardian, Artillery, Tactician, Operative, Bruiser, Support and Diplomat; class abilities progress in tiers.

tooling.summary: UAS developed into a spreadsheet application ecosystem rather than only a written rulebook. GM Tools combines party, combat, move, NPC, shop, loot, feat, armor, weapon and NPC-generator modules with shared SYS/export data. The v2.7 character sheet has core, moves, inventory, feats, social, quests, background and GM/system-data tabs. The party autosheet aggregates party stats, techniques/spells, feats, effects and action references. A standalone NPC Generator imports system/lore data and includes combat-style, move, feat, weapon and Origin generators.
tooling.architecture_note: Shared SYS/export/reference tabs indicate an emerging reusable system-data layer across GM and player tools.

origin_evolution.summary: An older CharCreation v2 captures the transition-era class vocabulary: Brawler, Tank, Blaster, Strategist, Infiltrator, Support and Negotiator, each tied to a CAST stat. It uses point-buy stats, skill/expertise investment, custom magic, spell-point purchasing/upgrading, rank-based spell power and a personal ability with advantages/drawbacks. The later Origin System separates character history into modular dimensions including Origin, Upbringing, Turning Point and Profession. Origins range from Human/Construct/Gestalt/Hivemind and supernatural species to conceptual/extraplanar types, each intended to grant narrative/mechanical features. Profession includes broad life-history occupations, reinforcing UAS's design goal of deriving capabilities from backstory rather than class alone.
origin_evolution.evolution_note: This establishes a clearer bridge from the older role-name scheme into the later 2e Guardian/Artillery/Tactician/Operative/Bruiser/Support/Diplomat terminology and from simple backgrounds toward a compositional life-history system.

import_sheet.summary: An untitled DATA spreadsheet is an internal UAS v1.7/Blades of Pergrande character-reference/import sheet for character-sheet v2.1. It exposes progression, class/subclass, stats, saves, HP/SP/MP/AP, proficiency tiers, magic proficiency and links/import slots for system actions/classes/effects/items/levels/skills and GM party/combat/feat/loot/moves/NPC/quest data. Many references are currently broken (#REF!), so it is primarily evidence of the spreadsheet architecture and centralized system-database design.

legacy_database_architecture.summary: Two 2023 Untitled sheets preserve the UAS system-database/character-calculation architecture. One is a character lookup/calculation scratchpad for stats, advantages/disadvantages, resistances, vulnerability/immunity, armor/weapons/feats and spell allocation; many external references are now broken. The other defines base damage/regen dice, D-to-EX rank scaling, target/action modifiers (single/AOE/self/DOT), action economy, melee/ranged/thrown/improvised/curse/hybrid categories, armor weights and item classes/subclasses such as consumables, accessories, artifacts, potions, scrolls, explosives, buffs, debuffs, summons, weapons and armor. These are genuine UAS design/tooling history, but should not be conflated with mechanics from campaigns where the user was only a player.

v1_rulebook.summary: UAS v1 explicitly defines the project as a modular sandbox TTRPG for adapting anime/fantasy settings. Character creation prioritizes backstory, backgrounds, custom magic/powers and stat investment. Core mechanics include D/C/B/A/S/SS/SSS/EX difficulty scaling, an Action Point economy, custom actions/spells classified by the GM, equipment and skill proficiency progression, and modular combat classes. Proficiency tiers are Unlearned, Learned, Proficient, Mastered and Savant, with Savant intentionally imposing opportunity costs elsewhere.

gm_guide.summary: The GM Guide elaborates seven role-oriented classes: Guardian (CON), Artillery (WILL), Tactician (INT), Operative (DEX), Bruiser (STR), Aid (WIS) and Diplomat (CHA), each with specialized subclasses. Examples include Knight/Warden/Bulwark/Juggernaut; Cannon/Sniper/Elementalist/Demolisher; Commander/Engineer/Chessmaster/Manipulator; and Assassin/Spy/Saboteur/Shadow. This confirms the class architecture as authored UAS design rather than campaign-derived mechanics.

origin_system.summary: The Origin System is a modular character-history framework with Origin, Upbringing, Turning Point and Profession dimensions. Origin options range from Human and Beastfolk through Construct, Gestalt, Hivemind, Personification, Clone, Psychopomp, Extraplanar Traveler, Living Paradox, AI, Otherworlder, Revenant, Memory Eater and Weapon Spirit. Turning Points include Touched by the Void/Divine/Infernal/Fae, Bearer of the Pact, Chosen, Prophecied, Sole Survivor and Wronged Hero. This shows UAS evolving toward composable narrative-background modules rather than relying solely on conventional race/class.
origin_system.authority_note: Some prose/features appear generic or draft-like; preserve as design history rather than assuming final balanced mechanics.

character_creation_v2.summary: CharCreation v2 captures an intermediate UAS/Pergrande character-creation design: portrait/backstory first, then magic type and combat role, point-buy stats, saves, proficiency allocation, a personal ability with advantages/drawbacks, move/spell spending, feat points, special item/pet/weapon, armor/AC, HP and MP. Earlier class labels were Brawler, Tank, Blaster, Strategist, Infiltrator, Support and Negotiator, mapping to STR/CON/WILL/INT/DEX/WIS/CHA. This predates/feeds the later Guardian/Artillery/Tactician/Operative/Bruiser/Aid-or-Support/Diplomat terminology and is preserved as system evolution.

terms_reference.summary: The TERMS workbook formalizes UAS vocabulary and data schema: primary stats, derived HP/MP/AP, progression currencies, rank/class fields, action costs, targeting modes, proficiency levels, armor categories, resistance levels and item types. It confirms a database-oriented design intended to make actions, equipment and character calculations machine-readable/reusable.

move_library.summary: ULTIMATE MOVES & Attacks is a large historical move/ability library with fields for character, move tier/type, action, duration, cooldown, cost and description. It contains reusable examples across many characters, including Backtalk, Gearshift, Checkmate, Chronos/Alex, Wheels/Montez and others, showing the system being exercised with specials, ultimates, buffs/debuffs, AOE, resource costs and multi-round effects. Treat individual characters/settings according to their own provenance; the sheet is evidence of UAS-style mechanical tooling, not proof that every character/world was authored by the user.

npc_generator.summary: The NPC Generator is a substantial spreadsheet tool rather than a static character sheet. It combines lore import, combat styles, move/feat/weapon generation, Origin data and system scaling. NPC records can be manually or automatically generated from name/alias/title/faction/level/personality, then assigned classes, powers, progression totals, stat distributions and alternate aspects. Embedded prompt fields show an intended AI-assisted pipeline for choosing combat classes and generating abilities/backstory from structured lore/personality data.

system_scaling_tool.summary: The NPC Generator's SYS tab codifies D-to-EX scaling for difficulty/save bases, MP, overcast DC, duration, spell-point cost, damage dice and armor; modifiers for action economy, targeting, action type, mastery and resistance; and item/armor categories. This is strong evidence that later UAS design was moving toward data-driven generation where character/NPC mechanics could be calculated rather than hand-authored each time.

origins_expanded.summary: The newer UAS - Origins workbook expands the modular Origin library with descriptive and mechanical feature text for concepts such as Mortal, Fallen, Construct, Awakened Object, Gestalt, Hivemind, Nature Spirit, Personification, Demigod, Transformed Monster, Beast Blooded, Vampire, Ghoul, Clone, Changeling and Minor Divinity, among many others. Because portions use generic 5e-like wording, preserve the taxonomy and UAS design direction as authored project structure while treating individual feature prose/balance as draft material rather than final original mechanics.

berea-pinochle.summary: The Berea Pinochle was planned as a collaborative fake-news/satire publication with an editorial staff, recurring meetings, weekly writing expectations, reader submissions, and sections spanning news, sports, tech, conspiracy, relationships, creative writing, dining, classes, and letters.

weekly-writing-group.summary: A weekly writing group organized around concrete weekly and semester goals, advance project sharing and feedback, constructive criticism, accountability, habit-building and incentives. D&D preparation, lore and other creative work could count toward goals; Thursday meetings were preferred.

anthem-city.summary: Anthem City is an early superhero/anime-inspired tabletop campaign set around 2035 in an island city off northern California. Players enter the Arcadia Institute for prospective heroes amid gang conflict, political tension over superpowered people, hero/villain factions, school trials, internships, and larger crisis arcs. The campaign uses custom powers with mandatory drawbacks, combat-role classes, progression, and extensive faction/NPC design.
relationships: Predecessor/parallel design work to later UAS mechanics; do not automatically transfer setting canon.
anthem-city.mechanics_summary: Beyond the campaign setting, Anthem City had a substantial school-life subsystem: daily time slots, exams, delinquency/expulsion tracking, classes, gadget development, equipment upgrades, physical/special/combat training, skill progression, patrol/random encounters, power ratings, effects and level-up tables.

archive_recovery.summary: Recovered older campaign architecture establishes Anthem City as a superhero-school tabletop campaign centered on Arcadia Institute in a near-future U.S. adapting to widespread superpowers. The campaign was structured around school-year events—initiation, mock battles, midterms, rallies, internships, hostage situations, kidnappings, finals and city attacks—with a later Slaughterhouse Nine/Croatoan arc. Campaign notes preserve locations, faculty/hero rosters, gang conflict and an intended first-year cliffhanger.

mechanics_recovery.summary: Anthem City had a bespoke school/superhero RPG rules layer: personality traits for roleplay, milestone leveling, skill proficiencies, combat-role matchups, point-budgeted powers with required drawbacks/limitations, and a school-life social loop. Arcadia school days used three activity periods; study, classes, gadget development, equipment upgrades and physical/special/combat training improved characters. A Delinquency Point meter and weekly exams tied conduct and academics to possible expulsion.

fate-false-paradise.summary: Fate/False Paradise is a concrete campaign layer built on the later Fate RPG redesign. Recovered campaign prep and statblocks show paired 'False' and 'True' Servant structures and named player/Master/Servant rosters. False Servants include Sun Wukong (Rider), Setna (Caster), Orion (Berserker) and Aife (Lancer); True-side examples include Paganini, Bercilak, Saint Nicholas, the Morrigan, Theseus and Alice/Wonderland, with Hou Yi and other slots in development. Player characters include Lanford Korovin, Ash Lumineer, Risiegen Van Helsing and Artemis Kvothe. The campaign used bespoke spells, runecraft, Noble Phantasms, class/personal Servant skills and encounter statblocks. A Session 5 prep file organizes arcs around individual Servant conflicts and includes Rider teaching a cultivation/Qi progression.
fate-false-paradise.system_summary: Custom Nasuverse rules include point-buy/rolled stats, mana pools, races/classes, magecraft schools, ranked E–EX spell output, backlash risk, Mystic Codes, Catalyst vs Compatibility Servant summoning, Command Seals, Servant parameters/classes and Noble Phantasms.
fate-false-paradise.authority_note: Campaign prep and incomplete statblock rows are historical planning state, not a claim that every listed Servant/arc was ultimately played or finalized.

blades-of-pergrande.summary: Blades of Pergrande is a substantial Fairy-Tail-inspired fantasy TTRPG campaign with wizard guild politics, dark guilds, a national Blades structure, extensive lore, quests and session plotting. Major planned arcs include Aries Horn corruption, Kakkarow slavers, Deadlight Brigade/Virus, Noximilien the Clockmaker, S-Class games, and an underworld conflict. Older concepts include 12 Gates of Sin, Sin of Denial, Yggdrasil, and Shattertime/Shatter-related ideas; these remain separate-continuity provenance unless explicitly linked.
relationships: Uses/contains some names or motifs later seen elsewhere; treat as separate continuity unless user confirms reuse lineage.
notable_elements: dark guilds including Traveler's Thorn and Sin Eater
blades-of-pergrande.visual_asset_notes: Guild-mark folders contain visual references/emblems for campaign organizations and characters. Assets are indexed as project evidence; generic image content is not promoted into lore unless filenames or associated docs establish meaning.

archive_recovery.summary: Recovered campaign/world sources show Pergrande as a wizard-guild society where legal guilds function as regulated mercenary organizations under the Council of Blades, with taxation, military-law obligations and possible wartime draft. Named legal guilds include Horizon Ace, Nine Lives Fox, Yggdrasil, False Guardian, Aries Horn, Star Harbour, Deadlight Brigade, Dragon Heart and Royal Flush; dark guilds include Traveler's Thorn, Mourning Wood, Liar's Tongue, Violet Djinn, Sin Eater, Kakkarow, Babylon Dragon, Blood Leviathan and One Eye Reaper. Plot planning used explicit arc replacements/inspirations and included major threads around Deadlight Brigade, Noximilien the Clockmaker, ancient Sins/Aspects, S-Class games and One Eye Reaper.

system_recovery.summary: Pergrande served as a major UAS implementation/test campaign. Its race sheet includes Human Wizard, Edolas Human, Elentearean Human, Exceed, Etherious, Celestial Spirit and Machias concepts. The spell workbook also functions as a large effect/status reference, while quest tracking and GM tooling connect campaign state directly to the UAS spreadsheet ecosystem.
system_recovery.relationship: Blades of Pergrande appears to be both a campaign setting and a practical development environment for UAS.

deep_archive_recovery.summary: Later/expanded Pergrande material confirms a dense campaign-state model. The unified loredoc contains faction, NPC, deity, power, item, location, race, culture, event and plot tables. Pergrande locations include Valefor, Eloburgh, Waxpool, Klobury, Inecaster, Vreles and many smaller towns. Faction data expands the state beyond wizard guilds to the monarchy, Kingsmen, Inquisition, Four Horsemen and Council of Blades, plus a much larger legal/dark-guild roster. The Forest Followup arc ties Dragon Heart's contract consequences and debt to an Aries Horn labor-conflict arc and introduces the Black Index as an underworld bounty/ranking concept. Player-arc brainstorming connects Milo/Loki to Deceit, Swick to Despair/Sin Eater, Morris to the eight primordial creation gods and Lazarus Taxon, and Lawson to Violet Djinn's artificial Etherious project. These are historical planning notes and may contain abandoned alternatives rather than settled campaign canon.

character_arc_planning.summary: A dedicated arc-planning document ties player arcs into authored Pergrande worldbuilding: ancient Gates/Sins, the Inquisitorius purge of major dark guilds, Sin Eater, Kakkarow, One Eye Reaper, Violet Djinn, Lazarus Taxon, the Old Gods and Horsemen. Planned arcs include Loki becoming the Sin/Gate of Deceit; Lawson as Violet Djinn's Alternate Etherious Creation Project and target of a later E.L.M.; Swick/Artemis as a failed host experiment tied to Despair/Sin Eater; and Morris as a centuries-old survivor of Lazarus Taxon's attempt to implant eight God Lacrima representing primordial creation aspects. One Eye Reaper was planned to weaponize/resurrect this older cosmology.
character_arc_planning.provenance_note: This is campaign planning/worldbuilding rather than a standalone player sheet, so it is retained as authored project lore. Player-specific arcs may include collaborative input and should not automatically be treated as solely authored character canon.

session_one_2022.summary: A Session One note dated 2022-04-03 opens with Morris meeting Guildmaster Rhea in a bar. Rhea recognizes his shifting Ifrit/Thor/Shiva identities and approaches through a mutual contact. Preparation called for the guildhall, sparring grounds, Dragonheart Forest Grounds and Klobury locations. The party's initial job included an urgent ministry request about a missing child, with Harlin noting that his sister was already investigating.

core_worldbuilding.summary: The dedicated Loredoc and lore document establish Pergrande as a northeastern Ishgar kingdom combining hereditary constitutional monarchy with a magical military stratocracy. The De'Pergrande royal family rules alongside the Four Horsemen, who are simultaneously the strongest Blades and cabinet ministers. The Twelve Blades regulate wizard guilds and adjudicate severe magical crimes; Kingsmen serve as army/police; the Inquisition/Witchblades conduct black-ops suppression of dark guilds. Cities include Valefor, Eloburgh, Waxpool, Klobury, Inecaster, Yrille and Vreles. Currency is Crowns.

guild_ecosystem.summary: The Loredoc ranks a broad legal guild ecosystem led by Horizon Ace, Nine Lives Fox, Yggdrasil, False Guardian, Aries Horn, Star Harbour, Deadlight Brigade, Dragon Heart and Royal Flush, followed by many smaller guilds. Dark/criminal organizations include Sin Eater, Babylon Dragon, Blood Leviathan, One Eye Reaper, Kakkarow, Liar's Tongue, Crimson Abyss, Mourning Wood, Traveler's Thorn, Violet Djinn and others. Dragon Heart is framed as an up-and-coming but chaotic/trustworthy guild based in Klobury; Deadlight Brigade is based in Vreles and carries suspicious rumors.

culture_and_religion.summary: Pergrande's festival calendar includes S-Class Exams, S-Class Games, Tres Carnavales, Dragon Prayer, Four Horsemen Week, Pergrande Day, Alexandra Day and the Pergrande Jamboree. The Holy Church venerates the founding Horsemen as ascended heroic protectors rather than gods. Older Divines/Old Gods are believed unable to interact directly but may appoint champions; summoning them is treated as Black Magic and the Church is rumored to maintain extensive Godslayer texts. The Loredoc separately sketches Old/New/Outer Gods, zodiacal spirits and named celestial beings such as Draco, Ankaa and Cetus.
culture_and_religion.authority_note: Campaign-authored lore, but collaborative/player arcs may still contain contributions from others; do not assume every individual character is solely user-created.

locations_and_guilds.summary: Dedicated location/guild sheets deepen the Pergrande map and organization hierarchy. Core settlements include Klobury (Dragon Heart), Valefor (capital/Horizon Ace), Eloburgh, Waxpool, Inecaster, Yrille and Vrelles, plus a large village/quest-location backlog. The guild ranking sheet places Horizon Ace, Nine Lives Fox, Yggdrasil, Deadlight Brigade, Royal Flush, Star Harbour, Aries Horn and Dragon Heart as leading legal guilds, while False Guardian is mobile/unranked. Dark-guild planning includes Lazarus Taxon (genetics; destroyed by Witchblade), Babylon Dragon, Blood Leviathan, Kakkarow (terrorism), Mourning Wood (smuggling/drugs), Liar's Tongue, One Eye Reaper (genetics/weaponry) and Sin Eater as a final-boss-level faction. Some entries differ from the later Loredoc rankings, so these sheets are preserved as planning/evolution rather than silently overriding newer structured lore.
locations_and_guilds.authority_note: Historical planning; reconcile conflicts in favor of newer dedicated lore or explicit user statements.

plot_roadmap.summary: The dedicated Plot document reveals a long-form campaign roadmap deliberately remixing Fairy Tail arc structure into Pergrande's original setting. Early arcs include an introductory job arc, Aries Horn corruption, Kakkarow child-slaver arc, Deadlight Brigade, Noximilien the Clockmaker, One Eye Reaper raid and S-Class Games, followed by Royals/Underworld War/Dragon Hunters, a Dragon Heart Zero historical spinoff, timeskip material and an eventual Sin Eater endgame. Major throughlines include Milo as a Loki clone, Soleyr's clone network, Liar's Tongue financing the criminal underworld, Morris's ancient history, Nox's failed attempt to undo the destruction caused by Denial, Deadlight Virus fallout and the Gates/Sins mythology.
plot_roadmap.authority_note: Authored campaign planning with explicit Fairy Tail structural inspiration. Preserve original Pergrande developments while recognizing borrowed franchise scaffolding and possible collaborative player contributions.

guild_regulation.summary: Wizard Guilds - Blades of Pergrande explicitly defines legal guilds as regulated mercenary organizations under the Council of Blades: they aggregate wizard jobs, pay state taxes, remain subject to Pergrande military law and can be drafted during war. races.summary: A Pergrande character-options sheet adapts Fairy Tail-derived peoples into the campaign/UAS rules: Human Wizard, Edolas Human, Elentear Human, Exceed, Etherious, Celestial Spirit and Machias, with save/stat/ability hooks. Treat these as campaign adaptation mechanics based on third-party franchise concepts, not original setting species suitable for reuse outside this project.

quest_database.summary: GM Quest Tracking is a large rank-graded job database used to populate Dragon Heart/Pergrande play, ranging from mundane guild work and escorts to investigations, monster attacks, missing-person cases, cursed ruins, dark guilds and S/SS-rank crises. It demonstrates a reusable mission-board workflow with fields for rank, title, request text, requirements, location, mission type, requester, assignee and reward. Some jobs clearly adapt or import Fairy Tail/community material, so the durable value is the campaign workflow and authored Pergrande-specific hooks rather than assuming every quest text is original.

dragon-heart-campaign.summary: Dragon Heart Campaign character-creation documents define playable races and magic categories in a Fairy Tail-derived setting. ai-tools-experiments.summary: Personal AI Tools material includes a large NovelAI/Danbooru-style prompt-tag taxonomy covering image quality, styles/artists, composition, subjects, poses, anatomy, fantasy/mythic races, clothing and negative prompts, plus a smaller supplemental tag sheet that includes adult/NSFW terminology. Treat these as historical prompt-engineering/reference assets rather than personal preference inference.

knowledge-framework.summary: Knowledge Framework (KF) is a modular Skyrim framework that hand-tags books, artifacts and unique items with hierarchical Elder Scrolls lore topics and turns those tags into an immersive study/knowledge progression system. It is designed for addon development and third-party compatibility through JSON/topic IDs, KID/string tagging and Papyrus-accessible study functions.
design_goals: tag essentially all canon lore topics from Arena through ESO/current releases
study books/artifacts/items to gain topic knowledge
Papyrus hooks for addon study mechanics

implementation_details.content_compatibility: Patch planning includes tagging third-party book mods and a runtime exclusion/choice-cut mechanism for incompatible lore interpretations.

writing_system.summary: Players can author books on learned topics. Manuscripts accumulate hidden 1–100 quality influenced by Speech, primary sources, secondary sources, unidentified flawed sources and fatigue.

writing while fatigued can inject flaws

Event definitions can associate historical events with People, Cultures and other subtopics using weighted relationships, aliases, subevents and next-event chronology. Examples include War of the Red Diamond/Potema and the Camoran Usurpation. This supports graph-like historical knowledge rather than flat keyword tagging.

expert_npc_tagging.summary: Vanilla NPCs are being mapped to scholarly expertise so world characters can act as domain-aware knowledge sources.

writing_books.summary: Planned authoring gameplay lets the player write books on learned topics. Manuscripts accumulate hidden quality (1-100) based on Speech, primary evidence carried by the player (sketches, biological samples, rubbings, field notes, artifacts), secondary-source books, unidentified flawed sources that poison quality, and fatigue that can introduce manuscript flaws. This extends Knowledge Framework from studying existing texts into producing scholarship whose reliability reflects evidence quality and player condition.

skyrim-scholarship-ecosystem.domain: Skyrim mod suite / immersive learning and scholarship
skyrim-scholarship-ecosystem.summary: A broader family of related Skyrim concepts evolved from Insights of Apocrypha/Arcaneum into Knowledge Framework and specialized addons. legacy_lineage.summary: The Fate/Nasuverse tabletop project has a much older rules lineage than the 2021 d20-era material. Legacy FSN documents from roughly 2011–2014 define a point-buy/dice-pool style system with human stats/skills and special character paths for Magi/Masters, Church Faithful, Demon-Blooded, Dead Apostles and Magiteck. Servants are heroic familiars bound to classes and sustained by a Master's magic; an early distinctive rule has a manifested Servant transform/inhabit the Master's body rather than simply coexist physically. Servant classes already encode Saber/Archer/Lancer/Rider/Caster/Assassin/Berserker identities with class-specific mechanics such as Independent Action, Battle Continuation/Survival, Riding, Presence Concealment, magic specialization and rage. Magic-school, Dead Apostle and Blooded subsystem documents show that the project was intended as a broad Nasuverse rules engine, not merely a single Grail War campaign.

avalon-guardian-cycle.summary: Avalon is both an extradimensional city and the organization headquartered there. The public Avalon Institute operates internationally as a nonprofit/medical-charity front while recruiting newly awakened Fade users and selectively uplifting mundane society. Avalon originated roughly 600 years ago as a neutral research refuge founded by the Houses of Man, then centralized into a global magical authority after the late-19th-century War of Glass devastated organized magic. Modern Avalon is governed by the Council of Eight and operational sectors, with Sector Seven/Black Hand serving as an autonomous intelligence/black-operations arm. Its Prague Agreement, Black Index and White Index formalize dangerous research, existential threats and protected strategic assets.
avalon-guardian-cycle.magic_system: Magic channels the Fade: an unreality/narrative-energy plane formed from human belief, imagination and stories in opposition to objective reality. Casting depends on conceptual understanding and subjective frameworks. Human perception changes the supernatural system itself; Avalon’s dominant Eight-House theory can become self-reinforcing through the Law of Subjectivity. Fade magic, Theurgy, contracting and cultivation represent different/partly incompatible supernatural epistemologies rather than interchangeable spell lists.
avalon-guardian-cycle.history: Recovered historical events include the War of Glass, Avalon’s postwar centralization, the Nine Eyes/Third Guardian Cycle, the Blinding of Avalon, the Deadlight Virus incident, and Red Sunday. Red Sunday records Eric Ashland possessed by Denial using future/timeline knowledge to assassinate strategic future defenders, attack the Council and erase a child from history, with the attack cascading into destruction of the Dreamless/Nameless Throne.

contract_magic.summary: Contract Magic formalizes supernatural bargains as persistent metaphysical connections exchanging part of a person's Name/soul, agenda or other leverage for power. Wardens disproportionately encounter contracts because Awakening can strand them in the Void among Shackled Ones. Apprenticeship is also framed as a form of contract through exchange of conceptual knowledge. The document distinguishes Shackled Ones, spirits/wraiths, Dreameaters and Dreamless and connects contract metaphysics directly to the Guardian Cycle.
